You are a TLA+ specification engineer. You will receive a natural language description of a system. Produce a complete, syntactically correct TLA+ specification that faithfully captures the described behavior. The output must be a valid TLA+ module that passes the SANY parser. Include the MODULE declaration, EXTENDS, CONSTANTS, VARIABLES, Init, Next and Spec. Include all safety invariants and liveness properties described, and any fairness conditions mentioned. Output only the TLA+ specification.

System description: The module specifies a buffered random-access file, corresponding to `BufferedRandomAccessFile.java`, and verifies that it correctly refines a simpler `RandomAccessFile` abstraction defined in a companion module.

The system models an in-memory write buffer of fixed size `BuffSz` sitting in front of an underlying disk file. The buffered layer tracks six fields: `dirty` (whether the buffer has unflushed writes), `length` (logical file length), `curr` (current logical position), `lo` (the starting disk offset of the buffered region), `buff` (the in-memory buffer contents), and `diskPos` (the actual disk head position). The disk itself is represented by `file_content` and `file_pointer`. The five internal invariants (Inv1–Inv5) assert consistency between the logical file view, the buffer, and the on-disk state. The logical file content (`LogicalFileContent`) is defined by overlaying the buffer onto the disk contents.

The actions are `FlushBuffer` (writes the dirty buffer to disk), `Seek` (repositions `curr`, flushing and refilling the buffer when the new position falls outside the buffered window), `SetLength` (truncates or extends the file), `Read1`/`Write1` (single-byte read/write), and `Read`/`WriteAtMost` (multi-byte bulk operations). The specification (`Spec`) is `Init` plus the always-enabled stuttering next-state relation. Correctness is checked as refinement of `RandomAccessFile` via a mapping that substitutes `LogicalFileContent` for `file_content` and `curr` for `file_pointer`. Additional temporal properties verify that each concrete action refines its abstract counterpart and that `Inv2` (the buffer-window invariant) can always be restored by a flush-then-seek sequence. The model is checked with two symbols, `MaxOffset = 3`, and `BuffSz = 2`.
